newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shows $210 mln trade surplus in January -TV.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shows $210 mln trade surplus in January -TV.

text.p: Brazil showed a $210 million trade surplus in January, with exports of $3.470 billion and imports of $3.260 billion, a local television reported.
TV Globo said the trade balance showed a surplus in January despite problems in the implementation of the Siscomex computerized system for imports, which hurt Brazilian purchases of goods abroad.
It said the problems were identified only in the first 10 days of the month.
Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper today also said Brazil may show a trade surplus in January but attributed the positive results to the Siscomex problems.
In the January 1-28 period, Brazil's trade balance posted a surplus of $222 million, the daily said.
The government had expected a trade deficit of between $500 million and $1.0 billion in January, Folha added.
A January surplus would be the first since May last year.
Brazil posted a record trade deficit of $5.5 billion in 1996.
TV Globo also said official figures for January trade balance would be released by Wednesday next week.
